name: Residence Permit for Employment

value.note: At least the average gross salary in Estonia for most categories, with published exceptions ranging from EUR 1,585/month (start-up employees, effective 6 March 2025) to EUR 2,972/month (top specialists); exact figures vary by employment category and change over time.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a salary at least equal to the average gross salary in Estonia, with lower or higher thresholds published for specific categories (e.g. start-up employees, top specialists).
requirements.fix_path: Secure an employment offer meeting the applicable salary threshold for your category.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires the Estonia-registered employer to hold an approval (recruitment permit) from the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund before hiring a foreign national.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract and employer's Unemployment Insurance Fund approval

outcome.duration_length: up to 5 years initially, extendable up to 10 years at a time
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: Extending a permit issued since July 2018 beyond 5 years requires demonstrating Estonian language proficiency at level A2.

sources.title: Police and Border Guard Board of Estonia (politsei.ee) -- Residence permit for employment

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Estonia's initial build. leads_to_pr and leads_to_citizenship are set false for this route ITSELF: the source page doesn't state that holding an employment permit automatically leads anywhere, but 5 years of legal residence under it is exactly what feeds ee_long_term_resident's own residence requirement -- modelled via switchable_to rather than asserting an automatic outcome on this file. The A2 language requirement at the 5-year extension mark is a genuinely distinctive detail (worth contrasting with ee_long_term_resident's separate B1 requirement) and is captured as a physical_presence_requirement-adjacent condition rather than invented as its own schema field, since the schema has no dedicated 'language requirement' slot. Salary thresholds are given as a note rather than a single resolved_amount formula value, since the source cites a range across categories rather than one figure -- flagged as thinner sourcing than a single clean number, worth a second pass with country-specific salary-category detail if this route gets revisited.
